[{"id":1,"user_id":5,"title":"The Dark Side of Matcha: Why This "Superfood" Might Not Be Worth the Hype","content":"Matcha has taken over cafés, TikTok feeds, and morning routines. Promoted as a clean, jitter-free source of energy packed with antioxidants, it feels like the ultimate wellness hack.
But behind the bright green aesthetic lies a different reality. For many people, matcha tastes bad, feels harsh on the body, and comes with a surprising list of downsides"},{"id":2,"user_id":1,"title":"MSN-04","content":"kasi cool?"},{"id":3,"user_id":1,"title":"Why Matcha Can Be Bad for Your Health","content":"• Digestive Distress: Tannins and the high concentration of EGCG can cause nausea, stomach upset, or heartburn, especially when consumed on an empty stomach.
• Caffeine Overload: Because you ingest the whole leaf rather than steeped water, matcha delivers a heavy dose of caffeine that can trigger jitters, anxiety, insomnia, or heart palpitations if overdone.
• Heavy Metal and Pesticide Risks: Tea plants absorb components directly from the soil. Low-grade or uncertified powders can sometimes contain trace amounts of lead or agricultural chemicals.
• Hidden Sugar in Commercial Lattes: Popular chain-store matcha lattes rely on massive amounts of artificial syrups and creamers to mask the harsh taste of cheap tea"},{"id":4,"user_id":2,"title":"blobloblobloblbolbog","content":"blologlhololho"}]
